body:
The Movement Needs a Method 

A field guide for the students at Jantar Mantar — and everyone who refuses to let the beating of children go unanswered

To every cockroach, plant, pigeon — and to all of Delhi's and India's students and parents: read this, sit with it, then move. Don't let delulu uncles and adults with zero good vibes go scot free after beating children. Convert passion into action.

Why this moment is different
The movement — CJP, Wangchuk, whatever comes next — was dying. Two things changed the mood and the timing altogether: Sonam Wangchuk's insistence on fasting with Ladakhi resilience, which delayed the cabinet reshuffle, and the Delhi Police beating children. Now everyone will head to Jantar Mantar, the way they did during India Against Corruption.

The beautiful bit is that this has no deep state planning — which is exactly why the Delhi Police, the MHA, and the Government of India are deeply afraid. They have never before been made fun of, or attacked, by their own future voters. This is a bunch of jokes gone right, riding algorithms over-indexed on American content.

The world — from the CIA to the KGB to Mossad — is probably watching this from their vantage points and embassy checkposts, waiting to see what happens. But right now, it is pure. It is a bunch of young people protesting the beating of kids. The vibe is real.

And even as the moment builds, the opponents of CJP — the people who want this quietened — are working multiple ends of the problem they created. The mass media, the billionaires, and the police are all with them. Young people have themselves, their parents, and their phones.

That is enough — if it is organized. There are two playbooks worth studying: Gene Sharp's 198 Methods of Nonviolent Action, and Srdja Popovic's Blueprint for Revolution.

First, immediate strategic ideas for the site and stage. Then the protest itself. Then broader ideas for the movement.

Part one: Fix the site and the stage first
Professionalize the physical space. Give someone from the events industry — EEMA, the people who run music festivals, the second-in-commands of the teams that produce film awards — charge of the protest site. They can do protests. Secure the site for passage flow, food, water, and toilets.

Build a high-quality digital presence from nearby. There is an online half of this movement, and it can be organized by people on the side. Digital and physical should talk to each other, but the best way to scale is to parallelize. Stay apolitical and all-political. Stay humble.

Run a daily public YouTube hangout. The world wants to know more and see more. Learn from Taiwan's digital democracy movement — how digital media and open processes were used to scale both ideas and organizing against a government. And assume the internet will be cut. Build human networks too.

Make the stage impossible to attack. Put an Indian Sign Language translator on stage. Surround it with people in wheelchairs, army veterans, monks, sages, old mothers, school students. Make it inconvenient for the constables and officers to carry out dastardly orders. Shame them into submission.

Never run out of ideas. Running out of ideas means running out of energy and support, which means regression to the status quo. Do innovative things from the stage and make them go viral.

Part two: The 198 methods, translated for India
Gene Sharp catalogued 198 methods of nonviolent action. Many are illegal in the Indian context — I'll let you think about those yourself. What follows are the legal ways to fight this moral war, across Sharp's three families: nonviolent protest and persuasion; social, economic, and political non-cooperation; and nonviolent intervention.

No more beating kids. Never. Bahut ho gaya.

SPEAK, WRITE, DECLARE
Public speeches. Hold "testimony" open mics outside the coaching hubs — Kota, Mukherjee Nagar — where students tell what a leaked exam costs: a year, a fee, a family's savings. Hold a "People's Convocation," with speeches delivered in graduation gowns, because leaked exams stole the real one.

Letters. Ten lakh handwritten postcards to the Education Ministry, each carrying just two lines: exam name, year lost. Open letters from parents — the constituency politicians fear most — published as paid classifieds in Hindi and regional dailies.

Institutional declarations. Get coaching institutes — whose business dies when exams lose credibility — to sign a joint Exam Integrity Charter. Get IIT and AIIMS alumni associations to issue statements: "Our degrees mean nothing if the entrance means nothing."

Signed public statements. Run a single Google-form petition, but print it and deliver it as a physical stack of paper measured in kilograms — "40 kg of signatures." Have retired UPSC members, ex-NTA officials, and former vice-chancellors sign a "Statement of the Examined."

A People's Chargesheet. Commission a formal, lawyer-drafted document listing every major leak since 2017. Table it publicly, deliver it to the Ministry, and publish it annually on the same date until demands are met. Make it a dreaded anniversary.

Mass petitions. Use the formal Petitions Committee of the Lok Sabha — few movements ever do, and it forces an official response. Collect village-panchayat resolutions from rural areas whose toppers were cheated; panchayat letterheads photograph beautifully.

SYMBOLS, IMAGES, SOUNDS
One symbol, one slogan. The symbol: a torn OMR sheet. Cheap, instantly legible, printable by anyone. The slogans: "Paper leak = future bleak." "Mehnat hamari, setting tumhari?" The image: a question paper flying out of a strongroom window — one picture, endlessly remixable.

Banners and posters. Posters listing only numbers — exams cancelled, students affected, convictions secured (usually zero). Let the last number do the work. Banner drops from hostel rooftops on results day.

Leaflets and books. A one-page "Know Your Exam Rights" leaflet distributed outside every test centre — protective, useful, and quietly radicalizing. A slim crowd-written paperback, Cancelled: fifty first-person accounts of leak-hit aspirants.

Your own press. A fortnightly aspirant newsletter — print plus WhatsApp PDF — tracking every pending leak investigation: a case-status tracker nobody in power wants to exist. Persuade education-page editors to run a standing "Days since last paper leak" counter.

Radio, TV, and song. Community radio spots in exam-hub towns. Short testimony clips. And a protest song — every Indian movement that lasted had one. Commission it from student musicians and release it results week.

Earthwriting. A human formation spelling "RE-EXAM" in a stadium or maidan, shot by drone, with permissions. Giant torn-OMR rangolis outside exam centres during festival season — unremovable by force without terrible optics.

Colors and badges. Adopt one color — say, answer-sheet blue — as ribbons, dupattas, and turbans on protest days; blue flags on hostel balconies nationwide on a declared date. The three main spokespersons can wear saffron, white, and green in rotation. A torn-OMR badge pinned to the chest at exams, interviews, convocations. Black armbands on results day for every cancelled exam.

Prayer. Interfaith sarva dharma prayer meets for "the future of the young" — it is very hard to lathi-charge a prayer. Havans, ardaas, and duas for exam integrity outside major temples, gurdwaras, and mosques, with priests, granthis, and imams invited to speak.

Destruction of one's own property. Publicly shredding one's own coaching notes and admit cards — own property only, safely, no fire. Symbolically tearing one's own rank card: "This number was stolen anyway."

Symbolic objects and lights. Deliver empty answer booklets to the Ministry: "You gave us nothing to write on." Send the Minister a single burnt candle per student — the midnight oil, wasted. Candlelight vigils on the anniversary of each big leak. A coordinated 11 pm "lights of the midnight oil" balcony-lamp moment nationwide, announced through aspirant Telegram groups.

Portraits — handled with utmost care. Portraits of students who died by suicide after cancelled exams, displayed only with family consent, with flowers, in silence, with dignity.

Paint, signs, sounds. Legal wall murals of the torn-OMR symbol in coaching towns, with owners' permission. Washable-chalk pavement stencils outside exam centres: "This exam brought to you by a leak?" Satirically rename the road to NTA headquarters "Leak Marg" with temporary, removable signage; rename aspirant WhatsApp and Telegram groups en masse to "Re-Exam Pending — Day 400." One minute of thali-banging at 9 pm on results day — a sound India already knows how to make together — and school bells rung outside the Ministry: the bell that should have started an honest exam.

Reclamation. "Reclaim the exam hall": book community halls and conduct a full, honest mock exam with invigilators, publicized as how it's supposed to work.

A note on discipline: skip the rude gestures and the protest disrobings — discipline is the brand; mockery yes, crudeness no. And skip personal taunting of officials: it backfires, invites cases, and dries up information leaking out of the system.

PRESENCE AND PRESSURE
"Haunting" officials. Lawfully attend every public appearance of responsible officials, wearing the badge, sitting silently in the front rows. No heckling. Just present. Always.

Fraternization. Befriend the constables on protest duty: share water, chai, and the one-page leaflet. Their kids write these exams too. Invite exam-centre staff and invigilators to tell their side — many are victims of the same broken system.

Vigils. All-night "study vigils" outside the Ministry: hundreds of students silently studying under lamps till dawn. The most photogenic protest in this whole document.

Picketing. Silent picket lines outside NTA offices holding only the admit cards of cancelled exams. And "study pickets": students sitting and visibly studying at the picket line. The image — we did our part — is the argument.

Deputations and lobbying. Small, disciplined delegations to every MP during session, carrying a one-page ask and a signature book recording who met them and who refused. A "Toppers' Deputation" of only students who scored in the 99th percentile in cancelled exams — hard to dismiss as failures venting. Systematic lobbying of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Education with written submissions, not just noise. And target the state education ministers of every party: leaks are gloriously non-partisan.

Nonviolent persistence. Sharp calls it nonviolent harassment; rename it persistence: the RTI flood, the daily question at every press conference, the standing question every MP gets in every constituency visit.

Humor as a weapon. Street plays: an auction where a question paper is sold to the highest bidder. A "leak-proof challenge" that publicly tests a steel tiffin box's seal against the exam strongrooms — the tiffin wins. A fake coaching ad promising "Rank 1 guaranteed — we know a guy." An annual Golden Leak Award for the institution with the worst exam-security record — trophy, citation, press release — and a "Lifetime Achievement in Looking Away" award delivered to the Ministry gate with cameras present. Nukkad natak troupes touring coaching hubs with a fifteen-minute leak play, ending every show by collecting signatures. A ghazal-and-rap evening: "Songs for the Waitlisted." Guerrilla theatre: two actors in "exam mafia" costume selling blank papers from a briefcase outside a metro station until a crowd gathers, then the reveal-banner drops. A "human strongroom" — students forming a locked square guarding a paper box, showing how easy real security would be.

Singing. Mass renditions of Saare Jahaan Se Achha outside exam offices — patriotic songs are unanswerable. Rewrite a well-known aspirant-culture song with campaign lyrics and let it spread as Reels.

Marches and processions. The March of the Admit Cards: each marcher holds their own laminated admit card overhead, nothing else, in silence. A relay march connecting coaching cities — Kota to Delhi — with the People's Chargesheet passed like a baton. A results-day Parade of Empty Chairs, for the seats never fairly filled. A shobha yatra or nagar kirtan themed on Saraswati, the goddess of learning, asking for honest exams — devotion as protest. A padyatra from a leak-affected village to the state capital, collecting testimony in a register at every stop, Gandhi-style. A slow two-wheeler rally through the coaching district — helmets, badges, lawful speed, no blocking, maximum visibility.

Mourning. A "funeral of merit": a bier carrying a giant OMR sheet, cremated with full solemnity — mock funerals of objects, never of persons. Annual homage at a memorial for students lost to exam-stress suicides, with families, quietly, no slogans. Some days the movement should only grieve. Wear white for a declared "Mourning of the Stolen Year" day.

Assemblies. A Students' Parliament in a maidan: elected aspirant delegates from every state debate and pass an Exam Reform Bill, live-streamed. Monthly mahapanchayat-style assemblies in leak-hit districts, with village elders presiding. Where permissions are obstructed, "study groups" and "career counselling seminars" can double as organizing meetings. And public teach-ins: a lawyer explains the 2024 anti-leak law, an ex-official explains how papers actually travel, an economist prices the leak economy. Free, open, recorded.

Silence and refusal. A coordinated walk-out from a Ministry webinar or townhall at a signal, badges left on the seats. A silent human chain around the NTA office — no slogans, mouths covered with white cloth marked "Cancelled." Toppers and medalists publicly returning certificates of exams later found compromised: "Take back the honor; give back the fairness." Audiences turning their backs in unison when officials rise to speak. Silent, legal, devastating.

NON-COOPERATION: SOCIAL, ECONOMIC, POLITICAL
Social pressure, used with care. Student bodies decline to invite implicated officials as chief guests to any campus event, anywhere, with public letters explaining why. University tournaments pause for one symbolic day: "No games till the exam game is fixed." Students decline to perform at official education-department functions.

The student strike, reinvented. A one-day national "class fast": attend campus, sit in the classroom, and study the People's Chargesheet instead of the syllabus. Rolling strikes, so no individual student loses much but the strike never ends institutionally. An "empty-classroom photo day" as a social media blitz. Break the social convention of silence: aspirants openly discussing their leak experiences is itself disobedience. Resign en masse from the ceremonial student advisory committees that exist to decorate ministry reports. And a "Ghar Baitho" day timed to a major education event — empty streets in coaching towns, shot from above.

Economic non-cooperation. Boycott the "guaranteed selection" merchandise and test-series products of any coaching brand caught colluding with leak mafias. A "No New Test Series" month, with the savings publicly pooled toward legal aid for leak cases. Photocopy shops and stationery stores in coaching hubs closing for one "No Paper Day" — the trade that lives on exams demanding honest ones. Coaching teachers refusing to teach "leak-prediction" content, and saying so publicly. Aspirants shifting accounts away from any bank found processing leak-mafia payments — only after verified reporting; no defamation. Instead of fee refusal, which invites direct penalty, the symbolic version: pay exam fees entirely in ₹1 coins, delivered in sacks, with a receipt demanded. Perfectly legal, unforgettable. And demand refunds for every cancelled exam through consumer forums, in thousands of parallel cases — lawful revenue pressure that also builds a legal record.

Rent withholding and similar contractual defaults create personal liability and aren't worth burdening kids with. The gentler version: PG and hostel tenants in Kota and Karol Bagh display "This room paid for a fair exam" posters instead.

Solidarity strikes. Coaching faculty stopping teaching for exactly one period nationwide, simultaneously, announced only an hour before. Ad-hoc invigilators and exam-centre contract staff — often unpaid for months — striking for wages and security reform. Junior doctors' associations, NEET-scarred, holding a one-hour pen-down in OPDs with patient care fully protected. Farmer unions in leak-hit states passing supporting resolutions. And the student-movement analog of the general strike: a General Strike of Attention — one day when every aspirant channel, page, and study group posts nothing but the demands. The algorithm as factory floor.

Work-to-rule from below. File every grievance through every official channel, exactly by the book, in maximum lawful volume — RTIs, CPGRAMS, consumer complaints. The machinery is designed to be used; use all of it. Never jam emergency or public services.

Hartal, the classic form. A voluntary one-day hartal in Kota or Mukherjee Nagar with the shopkeepers' consent — the Gandhian original, in the towns whose economy runs on exams.

Political non-cooperation. Publish a Legitimacy Ledger: a public statement that students will treat NTA results as provisional until an independent audit — words, not obstruction, fully legal. Boycott the Ministry's photo-op events — yoga days, felicitations — while attending every substantive hearing: starve the optics, feed the record. Refuse seats on toothless committees, publicly, with a one-line reason. Refuse to let student bodies be used to "manage" protests on the administration's behalf.

But never boycott elections. In a democracy, do the opposite: register aspirant voters and publish an Exam Integrity Scorecard for every MP before elections. Votes are the leverage; never surrender them.

NONVIOLENT INTERVENTION: BUILD THE ALTERNATIVE
The permitted dharna, upgraded. An indefinite dharna at a designated protest site with a daily 6 pm public "class" — turn the dharna into a free coaching centre. Occupation that gives. And "stand-ins" at NTA grievance offices: ticket-counter-style queues where everyone lawfully files a grievance, all day, every day.

The speak-in. At education conferences with open-mic Q&A, coordinated aspirants politely ask, one after another, the same three questions. Lawful, orderly, unbearable.

The reverse trial. Stage a full People's Tribunal on Paper Leaks: retired judges presiding, real lawyers arguing, real evidence from public records, a reasoned verdict published. India's civil society has done these well.

Endurance as argument. Study marathons in open maidans through winter nights: "We studied in the cold; you couldn't guard a strongroom."

New social patterns. Normalize "leak talk": a weekly open hour in every coaching institute where exam-integrity news is discussed without shame.

The reverse strike — the signature move. Instead of refusing work, do extra visible good work. Aspirants run free weekend teaching for underprivileged school kids under one banner: "We teach honestly. Ask why we protest."

Alternative institutions. Found a Students' Exam Integrity Commission — a real NGO with retired officials as trustees — that independently audits every major exam and publishes report cards. Build the institution you're demanding. Run a verified-news aspirant network — Telegram plus newsletter — that kills leak rumors and government spin with equal speed; become the trusted source. Publicly favor the coaching institutes, publishers, and platforms that sign and honor the Exam Integrity Charter — a whitelist is legally safer than a blacklist. Build a cooperative, at-cost test-series platform run by toppers, undercutting the leak-adjacent grey market for "guaranteed" papers.

Work on, without collaboration. Keep attending, keep studying, keep writing exams — while refusing every act of endorsement. No felicitations, no testimonial videos, no photo-ops. Full compliance, zero blessing.

Lawful dual sovereignty. The Students' Exam Integrity Commission, the People's Tribunal, and an Aspirants' Referendum — real polling booths in coaching hubs, results announced like election night, on one ballot question: Who should conduct exams — the current system or an independent commission? — together form a parallel accountability system whose reports become the standard the real system is measured against. That is dual sovereignty, done lawfully.

WHAT TO LEAVE ALONE — AND WHAT DEMANDS REAL DISCIPLINE
Don't do illegal stuff. Don't get overexcited; leave some stuff to the good adults, aunties and uncles you know. We are fighting incompetence and lack of conscience which makes it sad and easier than others. 

A few methods sit in between, and they demand the full Gandhian discipline or nothing at all. Refusing to disperse, sit-downs, courting arrest, and civil disobedience of "neutral" laws: if chosen, do it Gandhi's way — announced in advance, small trained groups, lawyers on standby, absolute nonviolence, courtesy to police. The arrest is the message. Never spring it on an untrained crowd. Challenging an unreasonable prohibitory order through disciplined defiance plus court petition is a legitimate, historied path — but it is a considered legal strategy, not a mood.

Whistleblowers inside exam bodies are the movement's most valuable allies. Build a lawful, protected channel — through lawyers, under whistleblower protections — for them to reach investigators and courts. Never induce anyone to break the law.

And the fast, the most Indian method of all, carries the highest risk — to health. If ever used: relay fasts only. Twelve-hour shifts, hundreds of participants, medical supervision — Sharp's "fast of moral pressure," never a life-endangering hunger strike. The movement needs its people alive and writing exams.

Part three: The people who make it work
These are all just ideas. Ideas matter. Execution matters. Luck is critical. But management and people matter the most. The core team matters the most: high integrity, high energy, high quality, zero ego.

The core does the risky, disciplined work. A small trained coordination cell of ten to fifteen that plans actions, holds message discipline, and vets every tactic against nonviolence. A legal cell of young lawyers plus one senior counsel for PILs, bail, RTIs, and cases. A treasurer and a public ledger — financial transparency is armor.

The mass base does the low-risk, high-volume work: badges, postcards, boycott days. Coaching-hub aspirants in Kota, Mukherjee Nagar, Prayagraj, Ashok Nagar, Anna Nagar. School students' councils and NSS/NCC-adjacent volunteer networks. Hostel and PG networks — aspirant central for India.

The shields protect everyone else. Parents' associations — the single most protective constituency. Retired officials: ex-UPSC members, former NTA and board officials, retired judges for the Tribunal, retired police officers who can advise on lawful assembly. Faith institutions — this work is dharma.

The amplifiers carry it. Edu-YouTubers and aspirant-influencers, the largest attention machine in this space. Stand-up comedians and meme pages for laughtivism. Student wings across party lines — invite all of them and privilege none; the moment this looks like one party's front, it dies. Regional-language journalists on the education beat — they break the leak stories anyway.

The specialists arm it. RTI activists — the paperwork artillery. Data and design volunteers for the trackers, scorecards, and the Integrity Commission's report cards. Musicians, theatre groups, muralists. Doctors' and junior doctors' associations, teachers' unions, invigilator and contract-staff unions. Coaching-industry insiders willing to sign the Charter — their business case for honest exams is your quiet superpower. And diaspora student bodies abroad, for solidarity vigils outside embassies: lawful in their countries, loud back home.

The last word
Show your work. Work in public. The next revolution will be live-streamed, and it will need physical and social networks so that it never depends on any one individual. People move on; systems endure. Men and women are mortal; ideas and legends are forever.

Fundamentally, remember: We The People. Government of, by, and for the people. They exist because of us — not the other way around. So you can, and should, claim your rightful powers back.

No more beating kids. Never. Bahut ho gaya.

VIDEO | Delhi: On Congress leaders’ protest at 7, LKM, party MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra (@priyankagandhi) says, “Do you think our democracy is being protected? What happened to us is irrelevant. We are standing with the students and raising their voice. What happened to the students, was it right or wrong? They are all young students. They are protesting, and this is not just any protest. It is a genuine issue, a genuine problem. Every parent in this country knows it. Every student in this country knows it. Every teacher in this country knows it. Everyone knows this is a genuine issue. The students are only asking for their rights…These students study with immense dedication and struggle to build a future for themselves. You are destroying that future. The entire education budget for the youth of this country is Rs 1.4 lakh crore. But you are writing off loans worth Rs 16 lakh crore for Adani ji and Ambani ji. The farmers get nothing, the poor get nothing, and the students get nothing.”

Regarding alleged attack on journalists during 20thJuly CJP protest, she says, “We are against violence. We always have been. This is the ideology of our party, and it is the ideology of our nation…I have also heard the protesters and students say that they are not going to resort to violence. So, if police personnel, journalists, or students have been injured, it is unfortunate. But please be truthful when you present these events to the public.”

दिल्ली पुलिस ने 20 जुलाई 2026 का CCTV फुटेज जारी किया है, जिसमें पार्लियामेंट के पास "कॉकरोच पार्टी अटैक" के दौरान की घटनाएँ दिखाई गई हैं।

फुटेज और पुलिस के बयान के अनुसार, हमलावरों को पार्लियामेंट की ओर बढ़ने की कोशिश करते समय बैरिकेड्स पर रोक दिया गया था। पुलिस की तैनाती के बावजूद, वीडियो में कुछ प्रदर्शनकारियों को कथित तौर पर बैरिकेड्स गिराते, उनके ऊपर से कूदते और आगे बढ़ते हुए दिखाया गया है। पुलिस ने कहा कि इसके कारण भीड़ को कंट्रोल करने के लिए लाठीचार्ज करना पड़ा।

अधिकारियों के बयान से साफ होता है कि टकराव तब शुरू हुआ जब प्रदर्शनकारियों ने बैरिकेड्स और पुलिस वालों पर हमला किया, न कि इसका उल्टा हुआ। 20/07/2026 12:35:00 का CCTV टाइमस्टैम्प उस पल को कैप्चर करता है जब हमला हुआ।

CJP प्रोटेस्ट, जिसे "अभिजीत दिपके" ने शुरू किया था, NEET 2026 पेपर लीक और एग्जामिनेशन सुधारों से जुड़ी मांगों को लेकर जंतर-मंतर पर चल रहा है। फुटेज जारी करने से पहले सोशल मीडिया पर उस दिन हिंसा किसने शुरू की, इस बारे में अलग-अलग बातें चल रही थीं।

दिल्ली पुलिस ने कहा कि यह कार्रवाई शांति बनाए रखने के लिए की गई थी।  कानून और व्यवस्था बनाए रखने और हाई-सिक्योरिटी ज़ोन के पास किसी भी तरह की हिंसा को रोकने के लिए।

Delhi Police has released CCTV footage from 20th July 2026 showing events during the "Cockroach  Party Attack near Parliament.

According to the footage and police statement, Attacker were stopped at barricades while attempting to move towards Parliament. Despite police deployment, the video shows some protesters allegedly bringing down the barricades, jumping over them, and moving forward. Police said this led to a lathi-charge to control the crowd.

The statement from authorities clarifies that the confrontation began after protesters attacked the barricades and police personnel, and not the other way around. The CCTV timestamp of 20/07/2026 12:35:00 captures the moment of the breach.

The CJP protest, founded by "Abhijit Dipke", has been ongoing at Jantar Mantar over demands related to the NEET 2026 paper leak and examination reforms. The release of footage comes amid conflicting narratives circulating on social media about who initiated the violence that day.

Delhi Police said the action was taken to maintain law and order and prevent a breach near a high-security zone.

body:
The NEET paper leak was one of the biggest betrayals of India's students.

Young aspirants lost a year of their lives. Some tragically lost hope altogether. The government, especially Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, should have acted with greater urgency and accountability from day one. Had responsibility been fixed early and transparently, perhaps this movement would never have reached this stage.

I have always believed that students have every constitutional and democratic right to protest peacefully for justice. They deserved support, not indifference.

But today, in my opinion, this no longer looks like a movement driven solely by students.

It appears that activists associated with CJP and individuals like Abhijeet Dipke have increasingly shaped the narrative, turning what began as a students' movement into a broader political campaign. When unrelated political issues, including speeches about restoring Article 370 from the protest stage, become part of a movement that began over NEET, it's fair to ask whether the original cause is being overshadowed.

If your fight is for NEET, keep the fight about NEET.

Damaging public property, escalating confrontation, and injecting unrelated political agendas only weaken the credibility of genuine students who simply want a fair education system.

The saddest part is that innocent students suffer the most. Politicians, activists, and ideological groups will eventually move on, but students alone will carry the burden of lost years, uncertainty and broken dreams.

India's students deserve justice.
They deserve accountability.
They deserve education, not political exploitation.

body:
The government was under the impression that re-conducting NEET alone would resolve students' grievances regarding the paper leak.

This is precisely why Cockroach Janta Party was ‘allowed’ to protest, and Sonam Wangchuk was ‘permitted’ to go on a hunger strike (who had done it 3 times before, albeit unsuccessfully).

In that way, Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan did not need to resign, and people would eventually move on to a different issue.

After all, it wasn’t the first time that an exam was compromised and generated public outrage.

The government hoped that the movement would fizzle out on its own. Because if it gave in to one demand, it might have to agree to others.

So, the government watched in silence as the number of protestors swelled. Sonam Wangchuk’s hunger strike crossed 3 weeks.

On social media, it became one man’s fight against the mighty State. This demand for accountability grew consistently.

People could freely back CJP as it did not have political baggage (Abhijeet Dipke’s connection to AAP appeared trivial before the core issue of the paper leak).

And for the first time in many years (after the CAA and farm laws), a protest had grown in magnitude unforeseen by the government.

The public resentment quadrupled after what transpired during the march to Parliament (only if you look beyond the echo chamber on Twitter).

It was clear that the indifference and lack of acknowledgement of the protests was no longer going to work.

As a result, Union Health Minister JP Nadda met not just the CJP spokespersons but also the students who were injured during the rally.

The core issue of the protest is non-political, even though many politicians and activists have frequented Jantar Mantar so far.

This is why I am seeing a large number of fence-sitters and apolitical folks throwing their weight behind Sonam Wangchuk.

You cannot convince anyone otherwise because it is too little and too late now.

Let us not forget that farm laws had to be rolled back and CAA remained in limbo for several years due to the large-scale protests.

Unless Dharmendra Pradhan resigns, this new wave of demonstrations is unlikely to stop.

Any further use of police force against students is going to make matters worse.

Despite heavy showers throughout the day on 21 July, hundreds of protesters remained at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, with more supporters continuing to arrive as the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) agitation entered another day.

Three key developments today:
• Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, along with other Congress MPs, staged a protest outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence, condemning the police crackdown on CJP protesters during Monday's march to Parliament and demanding accountability from the government.
• The Delhi High Court ordered that Sonam Wangchuk be shifted from Safdarjung Hospital to Medanta Hospital in Gurugram, allowing the activist to be transferred to a private hospital following a plea over his health.
• Addressing NDA MPs, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for rebuilding the trust of young people and emphasised the need for a foolproof examination system to prevent paper leaks such as NEET, as the government sought to respond to the ongoing protests. @hey_eshwar reports from Jantar Mantar.

body:
Why didn't #Vijay i.e. CM of TN support the 
#JantarMantarprotest ?

#CMVijay had already written to the #PM seeking steps to ban #NEET as soon as he became Chief Minister. So, his stand against #NEET is already clear.

Now, coming to the #CJP protest, it has three demands:
1. Release #SonamWangchuk 
2. Provide ₹1 crore compensation to the affected students' families.
3. Resignation of the Education Minister.

I agree with the first two demands. But I am skeptical about the third.

A paper leak occurred, investigations were conducted, those responsible were identified, and action was taken. The system is also being moved towards Computer-Based Tests with stronger encryption reduce such incidents.

If the demand was to #BanNEET because the system itself is flawed, we should support that. But demanding only a minister's resignation doesn't solve the root problem.

If #CMVijay supports this, it would set a dangerous precedent. Tomorrow, every issue could simply become a demand for a minister's resignation. Which is not justified !!!

Ministers can change. Unless the system is corrected, the same issue can happen again under someone else. 

I'm not a blind supporter of #CJP. I have my own reservations.

So, when I myself have doubts, I understand why #CMVijay chose not to comment.

That said, the protest should never have turned violent. The ruling Central Government i.e. #BJP must take responsibility for that.

POV : I'm not a #BJP supporter. This is simply my personal opinion.

@CMOTamilnadu @TVKVijayHQ

body:
Twenty-three days at Jantar Mantar, Delhi
Delhi is a prolonged, high-security standoff at the seat of national administration which doesn't read like a market shutdown. It reads like a signal about governance bandwidth. That's the real channel connecting this to the national picture: and the story keeps splitting into two different conversations.

The protest began over alleged exam-paper irregularities tied to NEET. It scaled sharply after activist Sonam Wangchuk joined on June 28 and began an indefinite hunger strike, drawing students, senior citizens, and civil-society groups whose core claim is that this is about institutional trust, not just one leaked paper.

Since then, security has scaled with it: five central Delhi Metro stations now shut entry and exit, and prohibitory orders cover the entire New Delhi district a daily operational cost for the businesses and commuters in that zone, regardless of anyone's politics.

Monday's march added a disputed chapter. Delhi Police allege protesters vandalized barricades and government vehicles and attacked officers, protesters and their supporters contest that account of how the violence started.

On the question of resolution: CJP representatives reportedly sought talks with a Union minister and offered names of ministers they'd meet, that proposal wasn't accepted, per reported accounts. 

What's certain, independent of how any of the above resolves: the commercial belt around the protest site absorbs the same daily cost, lost footfall, rerouted logistics, delayed meetings regardless of who's ultimately found to be right.

There's a layer to this, a street vendor near the barricades loses a working day because there's nowhere to set up. An e-rickshaw or auto driver loses their usual route and usual fares, informal-economy workers who don't have the option to "reroute" the way a formal business can. 

No official economic estimate exists yet for this protest specifically, traders in that single market estimated losses over ₹100 crore. That's not this protest's number, but it's the scale these things tend to reach once they run long.

For residents, the near-term future is more mundane than dramatic: continued rerouting, continued informal-economy income loss for those without the option to relocate their work, and a coaching/education sector that keeps deferring plans until the ministry question resolves.

#TamilNadu: A brief commotion was reported outside the Tamil Nadu Secretariat in Chennai after rapper #Arivu and four others raised slogans demanding the abolition of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (#NEET).

Police immediately intervened and detained Arivu along with the four others before taking them away for inquiry.

The protest comes a day after members of the Cockroach Janata Party (#CJP) staged a hunger strike and 'Sansad Chalo' march in New Delhi protesting leak of NEET paper. During a march towards Parliament, police used batons and tear gas to disperse the protesters, with several students reportedly sustaining injuries in the clashes.

Meanwhile, protests in Chennai also demanded scrapping the NEET exam.

Against this backdrop, Arivu's protest outside the Secretariat echoed the demand to abolish NEET, leading to his detention by Chennai police for questioning.

However, later, rapper #Arivu was escorted inside by officials from the Chief Minister's Office (CMO) to meet Chief Minister #JosephVijay.

By injecting politics into the protest and attempting to portray the students movement as one against the #TVKVijay‌ government, those who directed their hostility toward Chief Minister Vijay and the TVK administration have now been exposed by actress @ungalsanam.

At a time when the protest against the alleged #NEET question paper leak was meant to remain focused solely on that issue, some participants carried placards reading, 'We need JanaNayagam, not JanaNayagan,' thereby politicizing the students movement. Sanam Shetty has exposed what she describes as the agenda of DMK agents who sought to divert the protest for political purposes. While CJP members have been protesting in Delhi for over 20 days, many of those who had spent the same period discussing and celebrating the FIFA World Cup and new film releases suddenly chose to unleash their hostility when the subject became Vijay. Sanam Shetty has exposed the double standards of these individuals.

The students protest is gradually being diverted from its original purpose. Particularly in Tamilnadu, efforts are being made to steer it in a different direction. While the CJP protesters and the students are demanding only the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan, some individuals, unable to come to terms with their political defeat, are using the movement as an outlet for their resentment. By calling this out openly, Sanam Shetty has exposed these elements, and she deserves appreciation for doing so.

दिल्ली पुलिस ने 20 जुलाई 2026 का CCTV फुटेज जारी किया है, जिसमें पार्लियामेंट के पास "कॉकरोच पार्टी अटैक" के दौरान की घटनाएँ दिखाई गई हैं।

फुटेज और पुलिस के बयान के अनुसार, हमलावरों को पार्लियामेंट की ओर बढ़ने की कोशिश करते समय बैरिकेड्स पर रोक दिया गया था। पुलिस की तैनाती के बावजूद, वीडियो में कुछ प्रदर्शनकारियों को कथित तौर पर बैरिकेड्स गिराते, उनके ऊपर से कूदते और आगे बढ़ते हुए दिखाया गया है। पुलिस ने कहा कि इसके कारण भीड़ को कंट्रोल करने के लिए लाठीचार्ज करना पड़ा।

अधिकारियों के बयान से साफ होता है कि टकराव तब शुरू हुआ जब प्रदर्शनकारियों ने बैरिकेड्स और पुलिस वालों पर हमला किया, न कि इसका उल्टा हुआ। 20/07/2026 12:35:00 का CCTV टाइमस्टैम्प उस पल को कैप्चर करता है जब हमला हुआ।

CJP प्रोटेस्ट, जिसे "अभिजीत दिपके" ने शुरू किया था, NEET 2026 पेपर लीक और एग्जामिनेशन सुधारों से जुड़ी मांगों को लेकर जंतर-मंतर पर चल रहा है। फुटेज जारी करने से पहले सोशल मीडिया पर उस दिन हिंसा किसने शुरू की, इस बारे में अलग-अलग बातें चल रही थीं।

दिल्ली पुलिस ने कहा कि यह कार्रवाई शांति बनाए रखने के लिए की गई थी।  कानून और व्यवस्था बनाए रखने और हाई-सिक्योरिटी ज़ोन के पास किसी भी तरह की हिंसा को रोकने के लिए।

#कॉकरोचपार्टी #दिल्लीपुलिस #सीजेपी #दिल्लीन्यूज़

Delhi Police has released CCTV footage from 20th July 2026 showing events during the "Cockroach  Party Attack near Parliament.

According to the footage and police statement, Attacker were stopped at barricades while attempting to move towards Parliament. Despite police deployment, the video shows some protesters allegedly bringing down the barricades, jumping over them, and moving forward. Police said this led to a lathi-charge to control the crowd.

The statement from authorities clarifies that the confrontation began after protesters attacked the barricades and police personnel, and not the other way around. The CCTV timestamp of 20/07/2026 12:35:00 captures the moment of the breach.

The CJP protest, founded by "Abhijit Dipke", has been ongoing at Jantar Mantar over demands related to the NEET 2026 paper leak and examination reforms. The release of footage comes amid conflicting narratives circulating on social media about who initiated the violence that day.

Delhi Police said the action was taken to maintain law and order and prevent a breach near a high-security zone.

22. Who is CJP to demand the Prime Minister's resignation? He was democratically elected. What is the connection between his resignation and NEET?

23. What are the "usual suspects" doing at Jantar Mantar? Farooq Abdullah is demanding statehood for Jammu (amidst the NEET protest), Kejriwal is promising the best lawyers (who will pay for this, and for whom will the lawyers appear?), Akhilesh Yadav, and—as always—the Bollywood gang of anti-nationals (I wonder if any of their children have been affected). Dimple Yadav perhaps did not show as much sympathy for her husband, Akhilesh, as she did for certain "peaceful" protesters—a great photo opportunity for all involved.

24. Why did the top three "head cockroaches" vanish when the violence erupted? Was it not a convenient time for burgers, meetings, and the like?

25. Which minority group possesses such expertise in stone-pelting that truckloads of stones were seized? If this was meant to be a peaceful protest, what were trucks filled with stones doing there? And how much time, money, and effort does all this require? It could hardly have been a spur-of-the-moment decision; careful planning would have been the preferred route.

26. Why were truckloads of stones seized from CJP supporters? What were the stones for? They weren't ordinary stones but specially shaped ones designed to be thrown like boomerangs.

27. What was being carried in the CJP supporters' backpacks? Stones, undoubtedly.

28. Why were police vehicles and equipment destroyed? Who pays for this?

29. Why did the US State Department warn its citizens two days in advance—on July 19 and 20—to avoid the Jantar Mantar area? What did they know that we didn't? After all, the perpetrator always knows what is coming next.

ದೆಹಲಿ ಜಂತರ್‌ ಮಂತರ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತಿರುವ ಸಿಜೆಪಿ (CJP) ನೇತೃತ್ವದ ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿ-ಯುವಜನರ ಪ್ರತಿಭಟನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಜೆನ್‌ Z ಯುವಕರು ತಮ್ಮ ಆಕ್ರೋಶವನ್ನು ಕಲೆಯ ಮೂಲಕ ವ್ಯಕ್ತಪಡಿಸುತ್ತಿದ್ದಾರೆ. ಪೋಸ್ಟರ್‌ಗಳು, ಚಿತ್ರಕಲೆ, ಘೋಷಣೆಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಸೃಜನಾತ್ಮಕ ಅಭಿವ್ಯಕ್ತಿಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಆಡಳಿತದ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ತಮ್ಮ ಅಸಮಾಧಾನವನ್ನು ಹೊರಹಾಕುತ್ತಿದ್ದಾರೆ.

ಈ ಪ್ರತಿಭಟನೆಗೆ ಇಳಿವಯಸ್ಸಿನ ಮಕ್ಕಳು ಹಾಗೂ ಯುವಜನರೂ ಬೆಂಬಲ ಸೂಚಿಸಿದ್ದು, ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳ ಮೇಲಿನ ಪೊಲೀಸ್ ಕ್ರಮ ಮತ್ತು ಆಡಳಿತದ ನಡೆ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ತೀವ್ರ ಅಸಮಾಧಾನ ವ್ಯಕ್ತಪಡಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ. "ಮಕ್ಕಳನ್ನು ಮನಬಂದಂತೆ ಥಳಿಸಲಾಯಿತು. ಪ್ರಧಾನಿ ನರೇಂದ್ರ ಮೋದಿ ಅವರಿಗೆ ಸ್ವಲ್ಪವೂ ಕನಿಕರ ಇಲ್ಲ" ಎಂದು ಪ್ರತಿಭಟನಾಕಾರರು ಆಕ್ರೋಶ ವ್ಯಕ್ತಪಡಿಸಿದರು.

ದೆಹಲಿ ಸಿಜೆಪಿ ಪ್ರತಿಭಟನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಕೇಳಿಬಂದ ಯುವಜನರ ಧ್ವನಿ, ಕಲೆಯ ಮೂಲಕ ವ್ಯಕ್ತವಾದ ಪ್ರತಿರೋಧ ಮತ್ತು ಅಲ್ಲಿನ ವಾತಾವರಣವನ್ನು ಈ ವಿಡಿಯೋದಲ್ಲಿ ನೋಡಿ.

body:
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Friday hardened its stand in talks with the Centre, declaring that Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation remains a non-negotiable demand and warning that protests over the NEET paper leak would intensify if its demands are not met.

CJP spokespersons Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka held a two-hour meeting with Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh at Vithalbhai Patel House, the third round of discussions this week aimed at resolving the ongoing agitation.

The meeting came hours after the Union Cabinet cleared a draft bill proposing stricter punishment for paper leaks, following Prime Minister Narendra Modi's midnight video message announcing that the legislation would be introduced in Parliament.

Despite the move, Das said the "strictest action" would be Pradhan's removal. He said protests at Jantar Mantar would continue until the minister resigned.

In a letter submitted to the government, the CJP reiterated three "non-negotiable" demands: Pradhan's resignation, Rs 1 crore compensation for NEET victims and assurance of no legal action against protesters. It also sought public apologies from the government, the Rapid Action Force and the Delhi Police Commissioner over the alleged use of force against students during the July 20 protest.

Nadda said the ministers had heard the demands and would respond after further consultations. Another meeting is scheduled for Saturday.

The CJP also urged the Centre to consider its five-point charter on examination reforms, saying structural changes were essential to restore public confidence in the education system.

With protests continuing at Jantar Mantar, security has been tightened in the national capital. Additional CRPF companies have been airlifted to Delhi, while the CISF has curtailed leave for personnel deployed in the Delhi Metro. Internet and metro services were disrupted in several areas during the day.

The CJP also announced plans to launch a website to collect evidence of the July 20 police action and pursue legal proceedings against personnel accused of excesses. Meanwhile, the RAF said it had initiated an inquiry into allegations of disproportionate force during the crackdown.

body:
A day after Sonam Wangchuk ended his hunger strike, the protest is far from over.

Many had expected the agitation at Delhi's Jantar Mantar to wind down after Wangchuk called off his fast. Instead, thousands continue to throng the main protest site, while the roads outside Jantar Mantar remain packed with supporters from across the country.

Three key developments today:

• Sonam Wangchuk clarified his stand on Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, saying there has been no assurance or clarity from the government on that demand. He said he agreed to end his hunger strike after the government assured that no action would be taken against students who participated in the protests.

• The crackdown on protesters during the 20 July 'Sansad Chalo' march continued to reverberate in Parliament, with the issue triggering repeated disruptions and sharp exchanges between the Opposition and the government.

• CJP leaders who met government representatives reiterated that the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan remains their principal demand. He is Vibhu Gautam.

He made abusive remarks against the Indian Army during the CJP protest.

After his video went viral, some people decided that he should be handed over to the police. However, when they went to his house, they found out that his father is disabled. Seeing his father's situation, they decided not to pursue getting him arrested. Instead, they asked him to apologize, and he later recorded and posted a video apologizing.

Is it wrong to protest against the NEET paper leak or to demand the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan? No, not at all.

But that is not what he did. Instead, he came to the protest and started making abusive remarks against the Indian Army. He is not a child who cannot distinguish between right and wrong. He is old enough to understand the remarks he is making and the legal consequences of his actions.

His mindset led him to believe that it was the moment to turn India into another Nepal or Bangladesh. Many people like him also fail to understand that when they move away from the actual cause of a protest and engage in propaganda and anti-India activities, they may face serious legal consequences. Their careers and futures could be affected. In his case, even his father had to apologize because of his son's actions.

This period of unrest is temporary. The protests will eventually end. Those with political ambitions will move on and continue with politics. But common people like us may end up facing the consequences.

In the end, all that remains is regret.
By the time you realize the cost of your actions, the damage is already done. It can leave behind years of legal trouble, a damaged reputation, lost opportunities, and a burden that lasts far longer than the protest itself.

body:
Twenty-six days in, the last 48 hours showed how far this protest has spread-from the streets into digital infrastructure, and now toward a possible turning point.

Supporters across India and abroad had been sending food to protesters through Zomato and Swiggy in such large numbers that CJP asked people to pause orders for the day. On July 23, the government suspended mobile internet within a 1.5 km radius of Jantar Mantar until midnight. Around the same time, users reported glitches with Zomato and Swiggy in that area. Whether linked or not, the blackout had a measurable impact: UPI payments, deliveries, ride-hailing, and POS systems all slowed or failed, disrupting everyday transactions beyond the protest itself.

The same day, Section 163 was imposed outside Union Home Minister Amit Shah's residence, while opposition MPs protested at Gandhi Smriti. Reports also claimed the Centre had reached out for talks four times without a response from protest leaders, adding another layer to the disputed narrative.

Late that night, PM Modi addressed protesting students, calling the paper leak issue "not an ordinary matter" and promising stricter action in Friday's Cabinet meeting.

This morning, Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day fast at Medanta Hospital in the presence of Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh after losing nearly 11 kg. CJP said the fast may be over, but the movement continues, with demands for Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. Opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, continued their criticism.

What remains undeniable is that for 26 days, central Delhi has borne the cost, through disrupted roads, connectivity, and commerce. Those consequences extend beyond politics and are unlikely to disappear overnight.

You don’t need to be a NEET aspirant to stand with students.

You don’t need to be a parent, teacher or part of the education system to understand why education reforms and accountability matter-and why the protest at Jantar Mantar matters.

You don’t need to belong to a vulnerable community to defend its rights.

As a parent of a 24yr old non-verbal child, I have spent years seeking an inclusive, enabling environment where every child-irrespective of ability or disability-gets an opportunity to realise their potential and experience the joy of belonging.

Thousands of parents and advocates have spent years asking for implementation of laws already passed by Parliament and recognised by courts, including the RPWD Act.

But the biggest challenge remains: implementation of policies and accountability.

The same story repeats across sectors.

For 13 years, along with other citizens of Gurugram, I have worked on sustainable waste management and clean air through citizen initiatives like “Why Waste Your Waste”, “Stop Burning Waste: Let Kids Breathe” and Citizens For Clean Air (@cleanAirBharat ). 

We have policies on paper. Rules exist. Court orders exist but as paper tigers.

Citizens raise complaints, engage with authorities and elected representatives, but our voices fall on impervious ears.

There is NO JAWABDEHI.

Try dealing with a government department. Try seeking answers from elected representatives. The exhaustion of citizens and caregivers is real.

That is why we understand the anxiety, pain and frustration of the youth 

Many cannot leave their work and studies to stand on the streets. Many caregivers and older citizens cannot always be physically present.

But we can still show up.

We stand with the demand for #accountability.

Because the fight for accountability, dignity and good governance belongs to all of us.

The youth protest should make governments introspect-not only about education reforms, but why governance across sectors suffers from delays, inefficiency and lack of responsibility.

Whether it is education, disability rights, waste management, clean air, health or environment-the question remains:

Who is accountable when systems fail?

A truly #ViksitBharat cannot be built through slogans alone.

It needs policies that work, institutions that deliver and leaders who take responsibility.

Education reform is essential.
Governance reform is equally essential.

For every child. For every citizen.

Thank you #CJP @SauravDassss @abhijeet_dipke and several lakh students and Gen Z for the call to ACCOUNTABILITY-something every citizen deserves and India urgently needs. 🩵

CJP Protest पर Pakistan इतना खुश क्यों दिख रहा है?

इस 2 मिनट के वीडियो देखें और समझे....

दिल्ली के जंतर-मंतर पर चल रहा कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी का प्रदर्शन NEET पेपर लीक और शिक्षा व्यवस्था की खामियों के खिलाफ युवाओं का गुस्सा है। 

लेकिन सीमा पार से इसकी कवरेज और रिएक्शन देखकर लगता है जैसे पाकिस्तान में कोई त्योहार चल रहा हो।

भारत में किसी भी बड़े प्रदर्शन को पाकिस्तानी हैंडल्स और मीडिया तुरंत “भारत में अस्थिरता” के रूप में पेश करते हैं। 

हिंसा वाली क्लिप्स, पुलिस एक्शन और युवाओं के गुस्से को बढ़ा-चढ़ाकर दिखाया जाता है। दिल्ली पुलिस ने सैकड़ों पाकिस्तान-बेस्ड अकाउंट्स ब्लॉक भी किए हैं जो गलत सूचना फैला रहे थे।

“हम जैसे ही हैं” वाली सॉलिडैरिटी: कुछ पाकिस्तानी इन्फ्लुएंसर्स वीडियो बना रहे हैं कि “ये सिर्फ बच्चे हैं जो बेहतर देश चाहते हैं”, “हम भी वही झेलते हैं”। 

कुछ पोस्ट्स में जलन भी साफ दिखती है — “हमारे यहां ऐसा प्रदर्शन क्यों नहीं हो पाता?” यानी खुद अपनी व्यवस्था से नाराज होकर भारत के युवा आंदोलन को देखकर खुश हो रहे हैं।

 भारत में जितनी अशांति दिखे, उतना प्रचार। आधिकारिक तौर पर पाकिस्तान कह रहा है “यह भारत का आंतरिक मामला है”, लेकिन सोशल मीडिया पर खुशी और समर्थन का ट्रेंड अलग कहानी बयां कर रहा है।

VIDEO | Delhi: CJP delegation meets Union Ministers JP Nadda, Jitendra Singh. CJP spokesperson Saurav Das speaks to media after the meeting. He says, "Another issue we raised was that the Delhi Police has been detaining a large number of young men and women since last night, throughout the day, and even today. Those being detained include people leaving Jantar Mantar to return home, those heading towards the protest site, and even those delivering food. The police are selectively detaining young people and are also pushing and manhandling lawyers. We informed the government that this should not happen because it only deepens the trust deficit. The government's initial response was that no such incidents were taking place. However, it assured us that if such incidents are occurring, they would not be allowed to continue, and that the Delhi Police would be instructed accordingly.

CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka, says, "Regarding the main demand for the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan, the issue was discussed in detail with the government delegation. We conveyed in very clear terms that nothing short of Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation or his removal from the Union Cabinet would be acceptable. Across the country, protests are taking place in different places. There is widespread anger and resentment among the youth, and the sentiment is very clear... Nine years ago, S Anitha became the first victim of NEET in Tamil Nadu, and one of the most prominent faces of Tamil Nadu’s fight against NEET.

In 2017, the 17-year-old from Ariyalur had scored 1,176 out of 1,200 marks in her Class 12 Tamil Nadu State Board exams. Her medical cut-off score was 196.75 out of 200 — marks that would have placed her among medical aspirants under Tamil Nadu’s earlier admission system.

But that year, NEET became mandatory for medical admissions. Anitha, who had prepared through the state-board syllabus, could not secure a medical seat through the national entrance exam. She became one of the earliest voices opposing NEET in Tamil Nadu, arguing that a common entrance test would disadvantage students from rural areas, government schools and marginalised communities.

Anitha’s brother S. Manirathnam, who has now joined the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protest in Delhi, says her fight was deeply personal.

He says Anitha was raised by their father, a daily wage labourer, after their mother died when she was seven. He recalls that Anitha wanted to become a doctor because their mother’s death due to an illness had shaped her dream of entering medicine.

“She wanted to become a doctor because she had seen the suffering caused by the lack of medical care,” Manirathnam said, recalling his sister’s journey.

Anitha joined the legal battle against NEET and became one of the petitioners before the Supreme Court, seeking relief for Tamil Nadu students. The Court did not grant the exemption sought by the state, and days later, on 1 September 2017, Anitha died by suicide at her home in Ariyalur.

Speaking about the impact of NEET on his family, Manirathnam said, “NEET has destroyed my family.”

Years later, he has joined the CJP protest, saying Tamil Nadu’s opposition to NEET began with students like Anitha, who questioned whether a single national entrance exam could account for the inequalities faced by students across the country.

A video circulating from the Dadar solidarity protest organized by supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) movement shows a man identified as a police officer pushing aside a female demonstrator near a barricade while officers in yellow vests manage the crowd.

The footage has prompted political reactions, with Congress MP Varsha Eknath Gaikwad describing the incident as an instance of excessive police force and calling for the officer's suspension or prosecution.

Meanwhile, some social media users contend that the clip lacks context, arguing that it first shows the officer intervening with another protester before the interaction with the woman.

The CJP movement began as a satirical campaign in response to remarks about unemployment but has since broadened its focus to include issues such as the NEET examination paper leak and support for activist Sonam Wangchuk.

According to reports, Mumbai Police detained more than 300 protesters, citing the absence of permission for the demonstration.

body:
Activist Sonam Wangchuk on Wednesday ended his 26-day indefinite hunger strike after receiving assurances from the Centre and leaders across political parties that accountability for alleged examination paper leaks would be discussed in Parliament.

Wangchuk ended his fast at Safdarjung Hospital in the presence of Union Ministers J.P. Nadda and Jitendra Singh. Visuals showed Nadda offering him his first sip to break the fast, while Wangchuk's wife, Gitanjali Angmo, was by his side.

According to Wangchuk, the government also assured that the families of students who died by suicide following the recent NEET paper leak would receive adequate compensation and that no cases would be registered against students and youth who participated peacefully in the protests.

The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which has been leading the protest at Jantar Mantar, described the development as the "end of the hunger strike and the beginning of accountability."

Taking to Instagram, the man who goes by @adiespoems on the platform shared that he felt sad for not being able to join the ongoing Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest in Delhi. So, to show his support, he ordered 150 Domino's Farmhouse Cheese Burst pizzas worth ₹67,734 and instructed the delivery executive to distribute them to anyone who had not eaten.

@RahulGandhi ने सच में GEN Z को बेरोजगारी की आग में घी डालकर जगा दिया...

भाइयो-बहनों, GEN Z रुक नहीं रहा है। वो चुप नहीं बैठेगा। लाखों छात्र सड़कों पर हैं  NEET, NET, UPSC, SSC के पेपर लीक, भर्ती घोटालों और बेरोजगारी के खिलाफ। राहुल गांधी ने इन्हें vote chori = job chori का सीधा लिंक दिखाया, और अब ये आग पूरे देश में फैल रही है। जो चोर (literal और political) इसे divert करने की कोशिश कर रहे थे   Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, Arvind Kejriwal, Sonam Wangchuk, Abhijeet Dipke   सब नंगे हो गए। उनकी मुरादें पूरी नहीं होंगी। GEN Z जाग चुका है।

तथ्य बोलते हैं, भावनाएं नहीं..
45 साल का सबसे ऊंचा बेरोजगारी का स्तर...
राहुल ने बार-बार कहा  मोदी राज में युवा बेरोजगारी 45 साल के हाई पर पहुंची। PLFS और CMIE डेटा दिखाते हैं कि educated youth (graduates) में unemployment 11-13% के आसपास है, जबकि overall rate कम दिखाने की कोशिश की जाती है। Youth (15-29) में 9.9-15% तक joblessness, paper leaks ने 7.5 करोड़+ students को प्रभावित किया। 152+ major leaks, कोई सजा नहीं, सिर्फ lathi-charge।

Paper leaks और system collapse...
हर एग्जाम घोटाले में अरबों का खेल। छात्रों को मारपीट, detention। Rahul ने split-screen वीडियो दिखाया  एक तरफ Modi peacock feed कर रहे, yoga कर रहे, दूसरी तरफ police students को पीट रही। ये PR vs Reality है। GEN Z समझ गया: असली लड़ाई jobs की नहीं, vote theft की है जो corruption और failure को shield करती है।

Divert करने वाले नंगे क्यों हुए?
  Modi-Shah...
Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas का नारा, लेकिन manufacturing GDP share 15% से नीचे गिरा। 10 लाख+ govt vacancies खाली, करोड़ों applications पर मुश्किल से 0.3% selection। Ladakh में भी youth frustration 6 साल unemployment, statehood/Sixth Schedule की मांग। Violence भड़की, scapegoat बनाया गया।
  Arvind Kejriwal...
Delhi में unemployment eliminate kar denge 5 saal mein  का वादा, लेकिन ground reality अलग। AAP के अपने राज में भी youth gig jobs पर मजबूर। Rahul पर attack, लेकिन खुद jobs deliver नहीं कर पाए।
  Sonam Wangchuk...
 Ladakh में climate activist, लेकिन protests को his instigation बताकर divert। असल issue youth joblessness, unmet promises। वो खुद कह रहे ये organic frustration है, scapegoat मत बनाओ। लेकिन narrative shift करने की कोशिश फेल।
  Abhijeet Dipke (Cockroach Janta Party): Satirical movement शुरू किया unemployed youth के लिए। Viral हुआ, लेकिन mainstream politics में compromise या dilution की कोशिश? User ने ठीक कहा I support Sonam मत लिखो, murkh banoge। GEN Z अब individuals पर नहीं, systemic change पर focus कर रहा। CJP जैसे movements ने spark दिया, लेकिन Rahul ने national connect दिया।

GEN Z Nepal-Bangladesh style student protests देख रहा है। वो digitally connected है, satya और ahimsa से लड़ना चाहता है। Rahul ने कहा Your future is being stolen। सही कहा। 5 million graduates हर साल, लेकिन stable salaried jobs मुश्किल। Gig economy, unpaid work (खासकर women में 37%+), migration, frustration।

ये divert नहीं चलेगा...
Modi govt RBI/KLEMS data से 7-17 crore jobs claim करता है, लेकिन reality: educated unemployment high, LFPR में women unpaid work ज्यादा, youth disillusioned। Exam leaks में कोई conviction नहीं, सिर्फ students punished।
GEN Z को cheap data, reels, celebrity PR से नहीं बहकाया जा सकता। वो queue में खड़े होकर 40 vacancies के लिए stampede सह रहा है।

अब सच्चाई का समय...
Rahul Gandhi ने Bharat Jodo, पदयात्राओं से शुरू किया, अब Gen Z को democracy save करने का call दिया। ये nepo attack फेल हो गया। Youth समझ गया असली nepo तो power के चोर हैं जो institutions capture करके बैठे हैं।

GEN Z रुक नहीं रहा। Mela muraden मेरी मुरादें सफल नहीं होंगी। Protest जारी, awareness बढ़ रही। सबसे पहले सत्य साबित हो गया  Rahul ने जगाया, बाकी divert करने में लगे।

अब action चाहिए...
Education Minister resignation
Paper leak culprits पर strict action + exam reform
Massive job creation  manufacturing boost, skill + employment link
Caste census + equitable opportunities

जय हिंद। जय GEN Z। 
ये आंदोलन व्यक्तियों का नहीं, पीढ़ी का है। Constitution बचाओ, future बचाओ। Rahul Gandhi ने रास्ता दिखाया  अब GEN Z चलेगा...!!

अब समस्या ये थी कि आंदोलन में कोई आ नहीं रहा था तो उसको बढ़ाने के लिए सोनम को तैयार किया जाता है 

सोनम वांगचुग के नाम पर कुछ बच्चे आ जाते हैं मगर आंदोलन में कोई दम नहीं दिखाई देता , फिर रिप्लानिंग शुरू होती है 

JNU और आसपास के लेफ्ट विंग के आवारा खलिहर देशद्रोही टाइप लोगों को तैयार किया जाता है...उनसे मीटिंग के बाद पैसा वगैरह तय हो जाता है, डेली के 500 से लेकर 5000 तक बाँटे जाते हैं 

जो पढ़े लिखे बच्चे हैं और प्रोटेस्ट में शामिल होने आते हैं उनको शक ना हो इसलिए धर्मेंद्र प्रधान जी का इस्तीफा मांगने का काम शुरु किया जाता है 

फिर भी आंदोलन ना उठता देखकर आसपास के अपराधी माफियाओं को शामिल करके आगजनी दंगे का प्लान शुरू होता है....

संसद भवन घेरने का प्लान किया जाता है, जबकि उसमें दीपके, बर्गर खाने वाला दहिया और अन्य 2 मुख्य लोग अलग अलग डायरेक्शन में निकल जाते हैं ताकि जब आगजनी हो, सुनियोजित साजिश चल रही हो और पुलिस को गोली चलाने की नौबत आ जाए तो कुछ बच्चों की बलि चढ़ जाए...

दिल्ली पुलिस और संसद सुरक्षा में लगे जवानों पर बोतलों तलवारों से हमला किया जाता है, लूट जारी रहती है और पत्थरों का इस्तेमाल करके तोड़फोड़ जारी रहती है मकसद ये कि मजबूर होकर गोली चले और कुछ बच्चे मारे जाएं..

रोज कतर से लेकर बांग्लादेश तक से जोमेटो और स्विगी जैसे फूड ऐप्स का इस्तेमाल करके लाखों रुपयों का खाना आ रहा है, अपराधी चरित्र वालों को अनशन स्थल पर पैसा बांटा जाता रहा है..... प्रधानमंत्री मोदी जी की स्वर्गीय मां को गंदी गंदी गालियां, देश की सेना को गंदी गंदी गालियां सोशल मीडिया पर देशविरोधी बातें, भारत को नेपाल बना देने की धमकियां और जाने क्या क्या किया गया और इसकी वजह थी कि इनका प्लान सक्सेस नही हो पाया...

body:
Meme Turned Movement, What is the Cockroach Janta Party?

What began as an internet joke has become one of the most striking youth-led protest movements in India.

In May 2026, a Supreme Court hearing sparked controversy after remarks comparing certain unemployed people with questionable qualifications to “cockroaches” and “parasites.” Although the comments were later clarified as referring to those with fake degrees, many young Indians felt the insult landed on a generation already struggling with unemployment, exam uncertainty, and shrinking opportunities.

The next day, political communications strategist Abhijeet Dipke turned the insult into satire. He launched the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) online, asking in effect: what if all the “cockroaches” came together? With a self-mocking slogan; “Voice of the Lazy & Unemployed,” and a resilient cockroach mascot, the page spread rapidly across social media.

What made the movement different was that the joke stopped being just a joke. Anger over alleged NEET-UG exam paper leaks, exam cancellations, and broader concerns about fairness in India’s education system pushed the movement offline. Students gathered at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, and the protests grew into a wider expression of frustration about accountability, unemployment, and the pressure placed on young people.

The demands were direct: accountability for exam irregularities, reform of the public examination system, and the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. As demonstrations expanded, clashes with police, barricades, and reports of tear gas only increased national attention.

Supporters see the CJP as an authentic Gen Z movement that transformed humiliation into collective action. Critics argue it is politically influenced or disruptive. But regardless of where one stands, the movement has revealed something important: a generation fluent in memes and social media can also organize, mobilize, and force uncomfortable questions into the national conversation.

The Cockroach Janta Party is a symbol (half satire, half protest) that captured a deeper feeling among many young Indians: that they are tired of being dismissed, and ready to be heard.

So, have your social media feed algorithms changed?

Before 2024 elections when everyone was saying 350+, "400 paar", had said - BJP alliance together won't even touch 300.

𝘙𝘢𝘮 𝘔𝘢𝘯𝘥𝘪𝘳 theft issue - erosion of staunch Hindutva voter base.

Ethanol issue -  erosion of working/middle class voter.

UGC issue - erosion of upper castes, again a strong voter base.

Of all the above issues far more capable of cornering govt., CJP chose NEET paper leak. CJP did not choose it, they were destined to.
Just see the support it has been getting from different spheres. Map their ideological leanings with the issues above, you will understand why they would never touch those issues.

You think a peaceful would come on the streets for 𝘙𝘢𝘮 𝘔𝘢𝘯𝘥𝘪𝘳? A Leftist interested in upper castes? Or The First Family burning its bridges with a faction in BJP by raising issues that affect common man?

That explains, why NEET was chosen.

People have been at unease from past few months of lack of action by govt. on issues which are pending since 12 years - corruption cases not taken to conclusion, no communication, loose tongues within party badmouthing voters, no narrative building efforts, no ecosystem development.

When cockroach protest started, it was successfully thwarted because independent handles/supporters & not party/its affiliates/non-existent IT cell-PIB-MIB did the narrative counter & blunted the protest by digging up their all past history.

But when the Left-M axis revived it again after gauging overt anger among even voters of the government on above listed issues, the support base withdrew writing/supporting them. Abuses by some made matters worse.
Result: Government found itself completely cornered. Within a week, they realized how inefficient their communication is without this support base that writes & fights for them.

Now what after realization?

For the government:
PM himself has to intervene, issue video message. Some measures taken to resolve the issue.
Hope there is introspection to fix: communication & arrogance. Ministers have started conducting themselves as mirror image of PM Modi, copying him, & even harbouring aspirations of occupying his legacy. Take it as a word, none from the existing lot are seen by people worthy of it.

For the party:
Hope there is realization to create: ecosystem & strengthen ideological base by freeing itself within the framework defined by RSS or any organization. Loosen up & expand. Dissent must be welcomed & can be accommodated as a branch within the larger ideological tree. (Their supporters need to give up abuse & aggression towards dissenting voices).

For students protesting & 𝗺𝗼𝘀𝘁 𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗽𝗼𝘀𝘁, 𝗽𝗮𝘆 𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻:

1. If you are really a student leaving your exams & studies, & not a political party affiliate, then a folded hand request - vacate the protest site ASAP, & go home. Continuing any further can be detrimental not just to your academics, but a scar on your professional career for life. Sweeping actions are incoming laced with technology employed during Delhi riots. None of those vulgar messages, memes, & 15 seconds of fame has gone unnoticed. In the age of drones, face recognition, & AI tech you were playing to the hands of Leftist applause. 

2. This is no longer a students' protest. Though it never was but now it's overtly a political tug of war. Those celebrities joining in is such a give away.
Expect a split now - CJP & its initial support base (like Dhinchuk) know what's coming & would want to step away but their handlers won't. Political parties will pressure for this movement to go on. So if you are a genuine student, again repeating for your own good - go home.

3. Had started this post with a line - 𝘩𝘢𝘴 𝘺𝘰𝘶𝘳 𝘴𝘰𝘤𝘪𝘢𝘭 𝘮𝘦𝘥𝘪𝘢 𝘢𝘭𝘨𝘰𝘳𝘪𝘵𝘩𝘮 𝘤𝘩𝘢𝘯𝘨𝘦𝘥?
Expect some action on tech companies now.
Nationalists need to see how Western tech platforms can swing public opinion overnight, & should move to Indian alternates like 𝘈𝘳𝘢𝘵𝘵𝘢𝘪.
Also, some tech honchos running Leftist agenda through their 'philanthropic' funding disguise needs to be shut down now. Long rope given.

#IGR: CJP says protest to continue despite Wangchuk ending fast

The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) said its peaceful protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar will continue despite activist Sonam Wangchuk ending his 26-day hunger strike following talks with the Centre. 

In a statement, CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke thanked Wangchuk for his "extraordinary courage and sacrifice", saying his fast had awakened the conscience of the nation. The party reiterated that it would continue its agitation until Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns over the NEET paper leak controversy.

body:
OVERALL IMPLICATIONS - IS IT STILL ABOUT NEET ??
Throughout my walk, I encountered numerous placards, but only a handful were actually related to NEET. I even came across one on the Ram Mandir donation scam.

Overall, my impression is that Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation has become merely a symbolic demand.

The Gen Z protesters appear to be using it as a vehicle through which they are expressing a much broader set of grievances against the government. The protesters are not showing any signs of retreat. Instead, they seem to regard this as a once-in-a-generation political opportunity.

To me, it appears that the increasingly centralised and authoritarian style associated with Narendra Modi’s leadership may now be generating unintended political consequences.

The protesters are in no mood to negotiate.

More importantly, negotiations themselves seem destined to fail because there is no one with whom negotiations can functionally take place. Dipke and the So Called CJP has no hold over the Protesters

This movement is being driven far more by collective emotion than by structured political logic.

Governments may appeal to logic.
But it takes humanity to understand emotion.

And this, in my opinion, is precisely where Narendra Modi’s model of governance faces its greatest challenge.

The attitude that “इस सरकार में इस्तीफे नही होते” may once have projected decisiveness. Today, however, it increasingly appears to function as a political liability rather than an asset. It may even prove to be one of the factors contributing to the eventual Fall of the Narendra Modi Government

WHAT DOES THIS PROTEST MEAN FOR THE OPPOSITION, RAHUL GANDHI AND CONGRESS
This is a far more nuanced question, I will post a separate thread on that tomorrow.

CONCLUSION
I have no hesitation in saying that this movement deserves our faith and our hope. Something different, something unprecedented, and something genuinely unique is unfolding.

This is far larger than any political party or individual politician. What I witnessed today was a pure expression of “युवाशक्ति.”
I have never taken pride merely in belonging to a particular generation.

But today—
perhaps I should.

I will conclude with William Wordsworth’s famous reflection on the French Revolution:

“Bliss was it in that dawn to be alive,
But to be young was very heaven!” (3/3)

Delhi Police has intensified its investigation into the alleged violence during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protest in the national capital, with investigators set to analyse CCTV footage, drone videos, mobile phone recordings and other digital evidence to identify those involved.

According to police sources, multiple investigation teams have been formed to examine the available footage and identify individuals accused of attacking security personnel and damaging public property during the protest.

Officials are also trying to determine whether “outsiders” and “habitual offenders” infiltrated the demonstrations and contributed to the violence, beyond those already identified at the protest site.

Mobile Internet Suspended Near Jantar Mantar

Meanwhile, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has ordered the suspension of mobile internet services within a 1.5-kilometre radius of Jantar Mantar from 4 pm to midnight on Thursday.

The temporary restriction comes as security agencies continue monitoring the protest site and investigate the incidents of violence reported during the demonstrations over the alleged NEET paper leak.

Amid the ongoing student protests, Delhi Police on Thursday said it had identified and blocked around 480 Pakistan-based social media handles allegedly involved in spreading fake and misleading content related to the agitation.

In a video message, the police said the accounts were circulating misinformation to provoke people and distract students. It claimed that many of the identified handles were the same ones that had been active during Operation Sindoor.

Delhi Police appealed to students and the public not to share unverified posts, edited videos or content from anonymous social media accounts, urging them to verify information before forwarding it.

The statement comes as the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) protest at Jantar Mantar over the NEET paper leak and examination irregularities continues.

body:
The @Cockroachisback protest appears to have lost sight of its original objective and is now moving without a clear direction. (#NEETExamIssue #CJP) For the first 20 days, the protest remained peaceful, but it received very little media attention. It was only after the clash between the Delhi Police and CJP that the media began giving it significant coverage. Since then, the movement seems to have expanded beyond its initial purpose.

The original demands were for the Union Government to take accountability for the alleged NEET question paper leak and for Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign. However, the protest has since broadened to include demands such as Prime Minister Modi's resignation, the release of Umar Khalid, and the restoration of Article 370. These issues are unrelated to the core objective with which the protest began.

A similar shift can be seen in Tamilnadu. Initially, CJP's protests were peaceful and focused on the NEET issue. But after inviting several Instagram influencers who are perceived to lean towards the DMK, the narrative increasingly shifted towards criticizing the TVK government rather than focusing on the alleged NEET paper leak. There is also a fundamental difference in objectives. In Tamilnadu, many political parties, including TVK, seek the complete abolition of NEET. CJP, however, has primarily been demanding that NEET be conducted fairly and transparently, and that the Union Government be held accountable whenever irregularities or paper leaks occur. Mixing unrelated political demands with that objective risks diluting the movement's original purpose. 

It appeared that the Aam Aadmi Party was trying to capitalize on the CJP protest after losing power in Delhi to the BJP. However, Rahul Gandhi's protest outside the Prime Minister's residence seems to have changed the political dynamics. Since then, AAP's approach appears to have shifted, and some of its leaders and supporters have also begun criticizing the protestors and CJP, rather than backing the movement as strongly as before. Ironically, Congress's move seems to have given the BJP the political opening it was looking for on this issue. What began as a protest centered on seeking accountability has increasingly been framed as a Congress backed protest versus the BJP. As a result, the focus appears to have shifted from demanding accountability to a broader political confrontation, potentially overshadowing the original concerns that sparked the movement. @Wangchuk66 @GitanjaliAngmo @abhijeet_dipke
